metadata.citation: Ricker, N.L., 1996. Decentralized control of the Tennessee Eastman Challenge Process. Journal of Process Control, 6(4), pp.205-221.
metadata.description: Baseline decentralized control structure with 11 primary control loops
metadata.notes: Loops 1-7 are ratio controllers cascaded with flow controllers. Only the primary 11 loops are included here.

pairings.reasoning: Controls stripper liquid product flow (stream 11) to maintain production rate target with feedback adjustment
Uses product flow to control stripper bottoms liquid level, following downstream inventory control strategy
Controls separator liquid level using separator pot liquid flow, coordinated with stripper level to reduce product flow fluctuations
Controls reactor liquid level by adjusting condenser cooling to affect vapor carryover rate, as no direct liquid flows exist
Uses purge valve to control reactor pressure by balancing gas entry and exit rates, critical for safety and optimal operation
D feed rate controls product composition to maintain specified mol% G in product stream
A feed flow controls percentage of A relative to A+C in reactor feed to maintain excess reactants
A+C feed flow controls total A+C percentage in reactor feed to ensure reactants are in excess for rate-limiting control
Reactor cooling water flow controls reactor temperature to maintain selectivity and prevent thermal runaway
Condenser cooling water flow controls separator temperature as inner loop of cascade for reactor level control
E feed rate controls product composition to maintain specified mol% E in product stream
